summary.text: A giant planet is a type of planet much larger than Earth, usually made mostly of low-boiling-point materials rather than rock.
The Solar System has four: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, and Jupiter and Saturn are principally hydrogen and helium.
Uranus and Neptune consist of water, ammonia and methane, so many astronomers call them ice giants rather than gas giants.

facts.label: Term coined
facts.value: Gas giant, by James Blish in 1952

items.prompt: Why do some astronomers say 'fluid planet' would be a more accurate name than the usual nickname?

options.label: They are mostly liquid water with no air
They spin so fast that their matter flows
Most of their matter is under pressure too high to be gaseous
Their atmospheres are thick as oceans

items.explain: Throughout most of the volume the pressure is so high that matter is not in gaseous form.

items.prompt: Astronomers split the four giants into two pairs by what they are mostly made of. Which pairing is right?

options.label: Hydrogen and helium: Jupiter and Saturn; water, ammonia and methane: Uranus and Neptune
Hydrogen and helium: Jupiter and Neptune; water, ammonia and methane: Saturn and Uranus
Hydrogen and helium: Saturn and Uranus; water, ammonia and methane: Jupiter and Neptune
Hydrogen and helium: Uranus and Neptune; water, ammonia and methane: Jupiter and Saturn

items.explain: Jupiter and Saturn are principally hydrogen and helium, whilst Uranus and Neptune consist of water, ammonia and methane.

items.prompt: Astronomers find an object about 30 times Jupiter's mass that has started deuterium fusion. What is it usually called?

options.label: A hot Jupiter
A mega-Earth
An ice giant
A brown dwarf

items.explain: Objects big enough to start deuterium fusion, above about 13 Jupiter masses, are called brown dwarfs.

items.prompt: A probe approaches a giant planet, hoping to touch down. What will it find?

options.label: A hard surface just under the clouds
No true surface, only gas thinning into space
A calm liquid surface under the clouds
Solid ground only at the poles

items.explain: They lack surfaces altogether, since the gases simply thin out with distance from the centre.

items.prompt: Why were 'hot Jupiters' the most common exoplanets known for a long time?

options.label: They are the easiest to detect with ground-based instruments
They are the most common planets in the galaxy
They are the only planets space telescopes can see
They shine on their own like small stars

items.explain: Giant planets orbiting very close to their stars are the easiest exoplanets to detect, even from the ground.

items.prompt: Deep inside Jupiter and Saturn, hydrogen is called 'metallic'. What earns it the name?

options.label: It is mixed with iron and nickel
It shines like polished metal
It freezes solid like a metal ingot
Extreme pressure makes it conduct electricity

items.explain: The very high pressure turns hydrogen into an electrical conductor.
